_comment: Frozen ledger for the score-hierarchy audit method packet (item M2).
Every 'range' and every 'assumption' below is a HUMAN claim with a citation and a
proof method. The checker does arithmetic and drift detection only; it does not
derive bounds from Rust source and must never be described as if it did.
Citations: R:n = line n of the subject (sha256 98628e98...).

subject.role: AUTHORITATIVE for every question about what the shipped candidate scores

companion.role: AUTHORITATIVE only for questions about the dev-side sacred resident; NOT a source of evidence about the subject
companion.note: Different program from the subject. Routinely cited interchangeably in project documents. Any claim carrying a Y: citation is out of scope for a subject-level finding.

rules_authority.role: AUTHORITATIVE for what the engine does with an emitted command

bindings.claim: one reachable call site, base_score bound to the literal 6_000.0
one reachable call site, base_score bound to the literal 6_100.0
single call site; the producer of chop_turns for the RM-1 range model
two call sites; only R:477 feeds a score expression (RM-2)

range_models.note: Worked example A of the method packet. Reproduces the corrected chop bound (1500 base / 2400 with the absolute denial term). NOTE: the .max(1) clamp is reported DEAD whether or not chop_turns>=1 is propagated, because the `+1` literal alone forces the operand >= 1. Clamp-deadness is therefore NOT what catches the original manifest error; the propagated attainable interval of `turns` ([2,inf) vs [1,inf), giving 2400 vs 3900) is. See the packet, S2.5.

chop_turns.citation: R:566-570 via the single call site R:607
chop_turns.assumption: chop_outcome returns Some((turns,_)) only at R:569, inside `for turns in 1..=100` (R:566); every other path returns None and R:607 `let Some(..) else { continue }` discards it. THIS IS THE PRODUCER INVARIANT THE ORIGINAL MANIFEST FAILED TO PROPAGATE.

return_turns.assumption: ceil_div of a BFS distance or of a Manhattan fallback; both >= 0

wood.assumption: wood = final_size.min(free_capacity); `if wood<=0 { continue }` gives >=1; carry_capacity <= 3 from the shipped preset TUNED_CARRY max_carry_capacity:3 (R:327) and clamp(1,3) at R:850. UNRESOLVED for an initial roster shipping capacity > 3: then wood <= 4 (tree size cap, R:576) and the base bound rises to 2000.

opponent_distance.assumption: manhattan(plant.cell, view.shacks[1]) >= 0; the value 0 requires a tree standing on the enemy shack cell.

clamps.reading: `.max(1)` cannot change a value whose attainable interval starts at 2

range_models.note: Worked example B, step 1. `travel` occurs twice, so interval arithmetic loses precision; the checker labels this OVER_APPROX. The computed lower end 5817 is NOT proved attainable.

travel.method: panel-bounded assumption: corpus maps are <= 14x6 (fuzz/failures/m085-s0/candidate-transcript.txt:1-6), so a BFS distance is <= 83 cells and movement_speed >= 1

ticks_until_fruit.method: producer-invariant by loop-bound enumeration: returns 0 at R:411, or `turns` from `for turns in 1..=100` (R:416) at R:426, or the literal 100 at R:430

range_models.note: Worked example B, step 2. travel + max(ticks - travel, 0) == max(ticks, travel), so each variable occurs once and the checker reports EXACT. Both forms refute a closed 6000 lower boundary for the upper tier (chatgpt_1 review C3).
